bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-location geographic concentration of all manufacturing — The Sarora (Tilda) integrated facility, the Kuthrel facility and the Kesda greenfield land are all stated to lie within a 10-kilometre radius of the principal manufacturing unit in Chhattisgarh, and the Company presents itself as a fully integrated, single-location platform. Any local disruption affecting that one cluster would affect the entire value chain from sponge iron to finished pipes at once. This bundle does not contain a Risks and Concerns section; the risk is read off the disclosed footprint.
- Execution risk on the newly approved expansion, with no stated commissioning timeline — The Directors' Report records Board approval on May 09, 2026 of a H2,000.00 million capex to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route by 150,000 MTPA at the existing Sarora unit and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Sarora Unit-III. No completion or commissioning date is stated for either element, so progress cannot be tracked against a company-stated deadline.
- Growth funded by retained earnings rather than distribution — In view of ongoing expansion plans and the requirement to conserve resources for funding growth initiatives, the Board did not recommend any dividend for the year ended March 31, 2026 and decided to retain the entire profit for FY2025-26 in the statement of profit and loss. Shareholder returns are therefore wholly dependent on the expansion programme delivering.
- Dependence on third parties for contracted power arrangements — The Share Purchase Agreement relating to the Company's investment in CleanMax Opia Private Limited was terminated because CMOPL could not acquire the requisite land and obtain Stage II connectivity approval under the Energy Supply Agreement, and the Company divested its entire shareholding of 2,600 equity shares, with CMOPL ceasing to be an associate from May 30, 2025. This is a realised instance of a contracted external power arrangement failing on approvals.
- Dependence on the ramp-up of recently commissioned capacity — Both the Directors' Report and the corporate overview attribute FY 2025-26 revenue growth to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel and to the resulting shift in product mix. Earnings momentum is therefore tied to sustaining utilisation and market acceptance at facilities that have only recently started up.
- Reliance on a large contract workforce alongside permanent employees — As of March 31, 2026 the Company employed 2,303 permanent employees and 1,643 contract workers. The report states the workforce remains non-unionised and industrial relations were stable without significant labour-related disruptions, but roughly two-fifths of the workforce is engaged on a contract basis.
- Concentration of leadership in the founding family — The Company states it is led by promoters Brijlal Goyal, Suresh Kumar Goyal and Vikas Kumar Goyal, who collectively possess over 50 years of steel manufacturing experience, with the leadership team strengthened by Bhavesh Khetan as Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer. Strategic direction and execution rest on a small, related group of individuals.
- Short track record as a listed company — FY 2025-26 was the Company's first full financial year as a listed entity following its IPO and listing on NSE and BSE, so its disclosure, governance and capital-market track record is limited to a single completed year.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Vision 2030 is presented as an institutional growth framework rather than a project list, aligning capital allocation, manufacturing expansion, product diversification, operational excellence and financial prudence around a common long-term objective.
- Growth is sequenced in planned phases so that each investment is commissioned, stabilised and generating returns before the next phase begins, preserving balance sheet integrity and financial flexibility.
- Vision 2030 is to be funded with prioritised investment sequencing, conservative leverage and internal accrual-based funding, with the quantum of investment envisaged substantially higher than the capital deployed over the growth journey to date.
- Deliberate positioning in structural tubes, coated products and stainless steel - faster-growing, higher-value segments - rather than commodity steel, and building capabilities ahead of anticipated demand rather than reacting to it.
- Three pillars of competitive strength: specialisation in stainless steel, coated and specialised steel products; full backward integration at a single location; and energy security through captive power generation.
- Integration as a competitive advantage: deepen backward integration to strengthen supply-chain control and reduce input-cost volatility, and expand captive power generation to enhance energy security.
- Expand manufacturing scale: leapfrog production capacity, leverage available infrastructure, and increase finished steel capacity from 0.62 MMTPA to 2.03 MMTPA.
- Enhance value: increase stainless steel, coated steel and specialised steel product offerings, raise the share of value-added steel in the revenue mix, and enhance overall blended margins.
- Build a national steel brand: strengthen visibility around the 'Sab Sambhv Hai' campaign, build recognition through IPL partnerships, airport branding and digital engagement, and expand co-branding partnerships with stainless steel pipe manufacturers.
- Wider and deeper distribution footprint: deepen presence in high-growth domestic markets, establish an 'always around the corner' reputation, and help enhance the working capital efficiency of trade partners.
- Target a through-cycle franchise: protect and preserve market share in downcycles via margin resilience and cash-flow protection, and scale and accelerate in upcycles via faster response to demand and stronger pricing power, across ERW pipes, stainless steel coils and coated steel products.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company has grown by successive brownfield capacity additions at its Raipur, Chhattisgarh complex. Its key-milestones timeline records commencement of sponge iron manufacture in 2018 at 60,000 MTPA, expansion of sponge iron to 90,000 MTPA in 2019, commissioning of a 15 MW captive power plant (6 MW WHRB plus 9 MW AFBC) together with the start of blooms/slabs production at 120,000 MTPA in 2020, expansion of blooms/slabs to 150,000 MTPA and entry into hot rolled coils at 150,000 MTPA in 2022, an increase of blooms/slabs to 317,000 MTPA plus the start of Galvanized Iron (GI) pipe production and commissioning of a 132 kVA power line in 2023, and in 2024 sponge iron to 105,000 MTPA, blooms/slabs to 231,000 MTPA, HR coils to 350,000 MTPA and the start of ERW pipe manufacture at an initial 150,000 MTPA subsequently expanded to 250,000 MTPA. In 2025 sponge iron reached 280,000 MTPA, HR coils 390,000 MTPA and ERW pipes and structural tubes 350,000 MTPA, the captive power plant was enhanced to 25 MW (16 MW WHRB and 9 MW AFBC), the Company gained the capability to manufacture stainless steel blooms/slabs and stainless steel HR coils (60,000 MTPA) alongside stainless steel cold rolled coils (58,000 MTPA), and it commenced GP coils and GP pipes at 58,000 MTPA and 100,000 MTPA respectively. In 2026 the Company raised H440 crore and listed on the Indian stock exchanges; pre-galvanized (GP) coil installed capacity doubled from 58,000 MTPA to 1,16,000 MTPA; greenfield project execution started at Kesda; the Company signed an MoU with the Ministry of Steel under the PLI Scheme 1.2 for manufacturing stainless steel CR coils; and it undertook a brownfield capacity expansion from 58,000 MTPA to 116,000 MTPA for stainless steel (the report states this expansion range for stainless steel as well as for GP coils, and the two statements are not reconciled in the text supplied). Looking forward, the Directors' Report records that the Board, in its meeting held on May 09, 2026, approved a capex investment of H2,000.00 million to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route, adding 150,000 MTPA of production capacity at the existing Sarora unit, and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Village Sarora Unit-III, Tehsil-Tilda, Dist-Raipur, Chhattisgarh; no commissioning date is stated for either. Revenue growth during FY 2025-26 is attributed in part to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remains in the early stages of industrialisation, with per capita steel consumption of around 104 kilograms - less than half the global average - a gap management expects to narrow steadily over the coming decades, creating one of the world's longest visible steel demand runways.
- Domestic steel demand is described as moving towards 190-230 million tonnes by 2030, with the National Steel Policy targeting 300 MTPA steelmaking capacity.
- Specialised and value-added steel products are expected to grow faster than commodity steel; management argues value addition, integration and operational excellence, rather than manufacturing scale alone, will define competitiveness.
- Structural tubes and stainless steel continue to replace conventional materials across construction, water infrastructure, engineering and industrial applications on superior strength-to-weight ratio and efficiency.
- Stainless steel and coated products are seeing rising demand across automotive, railways, renewable energy, process industries and precision engineering on durability, corrosion resistance and life-cycle endurance.
- Mix is the key margin lever: value-added products contributed 92.66% of total revenue during FY 2025-26 (82.86% in FY 2024-25 and 80.05% in FY 2023-24), and the increasing contribution of value-added products enhanced blended realisations, enabling revenue growth to outpace volume growth.
- The commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel significantly expanded the addressable market while increasing availability of higher-value products.
- Highest-ever sales volume of 396,731 MT was achieved through expanding customer reach, improved production efficiencies and growing demand for value-added products.
- High capacity utilisation across key stainless steel facilities is cited as reflecting growing customer acceptance and as providing the rationale for the next phase of capacity expansion.
- A self-reinforcing cycle is described whereby demand growth raises the value-added share, higher value addition enhances profitability, and stronger profitability generates internal cash flows to fund the next phase of expansion, with backward integration retaining a greater proportion of earnings within the Company.
- Interest coverage improved to 5.43x in FY 2025-26 from 2.65x in FY 2024-25, supported by higher operating earnings and lower finance costs following the reduction in borrowings after the IPO.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sambhv Steel Tubes is a domestic manufacturer of ERW pipes, galvanized products and stainless steel coils, operating what it describes as the only single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures structural tubes and stainless steel products from two backward-integrated facilities in Raipur, Chhattisgarh, addressing the value chain from iron ore through sponge iron, blooms/slabs and HR coils to finished ERW black pipes, pre-galvanized coils and pipes, and stainless steel HRAP and CR coils. Sales are made largely through a distributor network of over 47 distributors serving more than 1,000 dealers, retailers and fabricators, with close engagement of EPC contractors, OEMs, infrastructure developers and fabricators.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains in the early stages of industrialisation, with per capita steel consumption of around 104 kilograms - less than half the global average - a gap management expects to narrow steadily over the coming decades, creating one of the world's longest visible steel demand runways.
- Domestic steel demand is described as moving towards 190-230 million tonnes by 2030, with the National Steel Policy targeting 300 MTPA steelmaking capacity.
- Specialised and value-added steel products are expected to grow faster than commodity steel; management argues value addition, integration and operational excellence, rather than manufacturing scale alone, will define competitiveness.
- Structural tubes and stainless steel continue to replace conventional materials across construction, water infrastructure, engineering and industrial applications on superior strength-to-weight ratio and efficiency.
- Stainless steel and coated products are seeing rising demand across automotive, railways, renewable energy, process industries and precision engineering on durability, corrosion resistance and life-cycle endurance.
- Mix is the key margin lever: value-added products contributed 92.66% of total revenue during FY 2025-26 (82.86% in FY 2024-25 and 80.05% in FY 2023-24), and the increasing contribution of value-added products enhanced blended realisations, enabling revenue growth to outpace volume growth.
- The commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel significantly expanded the addressable market while increasing availability of higher-value products.
- Highest-ever sales volume of 396,731 MT was achieved through expanding customer reach, improved production efficiencies and growing demand for value-added products.
- High capacity utilisation across key stainless steel facilities is cited as reflecting growing customer acceptance and as providing the rationale for the next phase of capacity expansion.
- A self-reinforcing cycle is described whereby demand growth raises the value-added share, higher value addition enhances profitability, and stronger profitability generates internal cash flows to fund the next phase of expansion, with backward integration retaining a greater proportion of earnings within the Company.
- Interest coverage improved to 5.43x in FY 2025-26 from 2.65x in FY 2024-25, supported by higher operating earnings and lower finance costs following the reduction in borrowings after the IPO.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has grown by successive brownfield capacity additions at its Raipur, Chhattisgarh complex. Its key-milestones timeline records commencement of sponge iron manufacture in 2018 at 60,000 MTPA, expansion of sponge iron to 90,000 MTPA in 2019, commissioning of a 15 MW captive power plant (6 MW WHRB plus 9 MW AFBC) together with the start of blooms/slabs production at 120,000 MTPA in 2020, expansion of blooms/slabs to 150,000 MTPA and entry into hot rolled coils at 150,000 MTPA in 2022, an increase of blooms/slabs to 317,000 MTPA plus the start of Galvanized Iron (GI) pipe production and commissioning of a 132 kVA power line in 2023, and in 2024 sponge iron to 105,000 MTPA, blooms/slabs to 231,000 MTPA, HR coils to 350,000 MTPA and the start of ERW pipe manufacture at an initial 150,000 MTPA subsequently expanded to 250,000 MTPA. In 2025 sponge iron reached 280,000 MTPA, HR coils 390,000 MTPA and ERW pipes and structural tubes 350,000 MTPA, the captive power plant was enhanced to 25 MW (16 MW WHRB and 9 MW AFBC), the Company gained the capability to manufacture stainless steel blooms/slabs and stainless steel HR coils (60,000 MTPA) alongside stainless steel cold rolled coils (58,000 MTPA), and it commenced GP coils and GP pipes at 58,000 MTPA and 100,000 MTPA respectively. In 2026 the Company raised H440 crore and listed on the Indian stock exchanges; pre-galvanized (GP) coil installed capacity doubled from 58,000 MTPA to 1,16,000 MTPA; greenfield project execution started at Kesda; the Company signed an MoU with the Ministry of Steel under the PLI Scheme 1.2 for manufacturing stainless steel CR coils; and it undertook a brownfield capacity expansion from 58,000 MTPA to 116,000 MTPA for stainless steel (the report states this expansion range for stainless steel as well as for GP coils, and the two statements are not reconciled in the text supplied). Looking forward, the Directors' Report records that the Board, in its meeting held on May 09, 2026, approved a capex investment of H2,000.00 million to expand the Pipe Mill via the DFT route, adding 150,000 MTPA of production capacity at the existing Sarora unit, and to set up an additional round-the-clock 30 MW captive power plant at Village Sarora Unit-III, Tehsil-Tilda, Dist-Raipur, Chhattisgarh; no commissioning date is stated for either. Revenue growth during FY 2025-26 is attributed in part to the commercial ramp-up of the newly commissioned stainless steel and pre-galvanized facilities at Kuthrel.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Described as the only Indian player with a single-location, fully backward-integrated ERW pipe facility, producing key intermediates such as sponge iron, slabs and HR coils in-house
- One of the few domestic producers of narrow-width hot rolled coils through a secondary steelmaking route (DRI plus induction furnace), which reduces capital expenditure in pipe manufacturing and dependence on external HR coil suppliers
- Among a limited number of manufacturers in India producing stainless steel blooms/slabs through the Argon Oxygen Decarburization (AOD) process, described as cost-effective
- Ladle Refining Furnace capability allows alloy steel production through the induction furnace route, including Corten steel pipes
- Advanced Non-Ox technology for pre-galvanized coils and pipes uses significantly less zinc, improving cost efficiency without compromising quality
- Captive WHRB and AFBC power plants utilise waste heat and by-products such as dolochar for power generation, the WHRB requiring no additional fuel
- Strategic location in Raipur, Chhattisgarh close to coal and high-grade iron ore, with iron ore sourced from a Navratna public sector enterprise and coal largely from a subsidiary of India's largest coal producer situated within 250 kms of the facilities
- Dealer-distributor network across 15 states and one Union Territory with over 47 distributors and more than 1,000 dealers, supporting stable double-digit operating margins
- Long-term ratings reaffirmed during FY 2025-26 at CARE A (Stable) and ACUITE A (Stable), with short-term ratings maintained at CARE A1 and ACUITE A1
